subject: In the output of INLA, what's the relationship between 'summary.fixed' and 'marginals.fixed', or between 'summary.random' and 'marginals.random'

messages.author: ff1a5632abbf2fe9
messages.subject: In the output of INLA, what's the relationship between 'summary.fixed' and 'marginals.fixed', or between 'summary.random' and 'marginals.random'
parts:
Hi,

Maybe a naive question
In the output of INLA,  every effect term, irrespective of fixed or random, has 27 pairs of 'x' and 'y' in the 'marginals.fixed'(or 'marginals.random')
How do the 'x' and'y' pairs come out? 
why 27? 
Do them have something to do with 'summary.fixed' (or 'summary.random')?


Best
Xing

just plot the x against the y values and you see. its the representation

what you see in summary.fixed/random is the summary statistics computed

messages.subject: Re: Re: [r-inla] In the output of INLA, what's the relationship between 'summary.fixed' and 'marginals.fixed', or between 'summary.random' and 'marginals.random'
parts:
That's what I thought at the beginning, but I cannot reproduce the result
The example for the function marginal {INLA} is (I give additional seed code for reproducibility ):
 
> ## a simple linear regression example
> n = 10
> set.seed(3.1415)
> x = rnorm(n)
> sd = 0.1
> set.seed(80)
> y = 1+x + rnorm(n,sd=sd)
> res = inla(y ~ 1 + x, data = data.frame(x,y),
+            control.family=list(initial = log(1/sd^2),fixed=TRUE))
> res$summary.fixed
                 mean         sd 0.025quant  0.5quant 0.975quant          kld
(Intercept) 1.0059903 0.03167083  0.9437226 1.0059901   1.068272 7.000882e-06
x           0.9996182 0.03853530  0.9240545 0.9996179   1.075198 3.650588e-17
> (res$marginals.fixed$x[,1] %*% res$marginals.fixed$x[,2])/sum(res$marginals.fixed$x[,2])
          [,1]
[1,] 0.9996186
 
For the posterior mean, they are 0.9996182 vs 0.9996186
Just numeric reason can explain?
 
 
 
 
ZhaoXing

probably it just returns 29 points:

more <- inla.smarginal(res$marginals.fixed$x,keep.type=T)
(more[,1] %*% more[,2])/sum(more[,2])

this gave the same value with the summary

best

Dear list

Working with some simple spatial BYM models I stumbled upon this topic.

When mapping results of the models in INLA tutorials I mainly saw (bym example for instance) summary being used.

result1$summary.random$region.struct$mean

In LondonSuicides.R example of Blangiardo et al (2012) marginals are used

m <- mod.cov$marginals.random$ID[1:Nareas]
zeta.cov <- lapply(m,function(x)inla.emarginal(exp,x))

Which of these two options is a prefered to be presented on maps?
